subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the coordinates of the point on the parabola y² = 8x whose focal distance is 10.

mark_split.label: Find a and set up the focal distance

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and set up the focal distance
steps.margin_note: First mark, for finding a and setting up x₁ + a = 10.
steps.why: The focal distance of any point on y² = 4ax is always x₁ + a — a fixed rule that turns the word 'focal distance' straight into an equation for x₁.
common_mistakes: Reading 4a from y² = 8x as a = 8 instead of a = 2.
Writing the focal distance as x₁ − a instead of x₁ + a.
steps.memory_tip: Focal distance is always x-coordinate plus a — SP = x₁ + a, for any point on y² = 4ax.

steps.label: Solve for the point
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for both coordinates of the point, with the ± sign.
steps.why: Once x₁ is known, y₁ follows straight from the parabola's own equation — and every x on this curve pairs with two values of y, one above the axis and one below.
common_mistakes: Giving only one value of y₁ and forgetting the ± sign.
Writing y₁ = 8x₁ instead of y₁² = 8x₁ before taking the square root.
steps.memory_tip: Every x on the curve gives two points, one above the axis and one below — always write the ± sign.

insider_note: The ± sign on y₁ is the easiest mark to drop in this question — the parabola is symmetric about its axis, so every valid x always gives two points.
